vector_index.answer: HNSW: the docs recommend it for large collections that need high query throughput and low latency, which 5 million products at high QPS are. Keep the defaults, including dynamic ef (ef = -1), and reduce memory with compression rather than a flat or dynamic index.

code.python:
from weaviate.classes.config import Configure, Property, DataType

# HNSW is the default index; 8-bit RQ is the default rq() quantizer.
client.collections.create(
    name="Product",
    vector_config=Configure.Vectors.text2vec_openai(
        model="text-embedding-3-small",
        quantizer=Configure.VectorIndex.Quantizer.rq(),
    ),
    properties=[
        Property(name="title", data_type=DataType.TEXT),
        Property(name="description", data_type=DataType.TEXT),
    ],
)

compression.answer: 8-bit rotational quantization (RQ): recommended for most use cases, about 4x compression with 98-99% recall, and no training step, so it is enabled when the collection is created.

batch_import.answer: Server-side batching, the recommended import: the server sets the rate the client sends at, so there are no batch sizes to tune. Python and TypeScript use data.ingest() with a generator or list; Go v6 uses collection.Batch(ctx, ...). The Go v5 client does not support it.
